    The Week Recommends

    The best disaster movies of all time

    Airports, asteroids and tsunamis star in these renditions of our worst fears

    By David Faris, The Week US
    Published 2 days ago
    • Facebook
    • X
    • Linkedin
    • Whatsapp
    • Pinterest
    • Instagram
    Share this article

    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:57
    Instaread

    Our enduring fascination with disasters both real and imagined has produced a never-ending string of box-office smashes. And the question of how humans respond to unexpected mass tragedies is thrillingly addressed in these four blockbusters.

    ‘Airport’ (1970)

    Airport (1970) ORIGINAL TRAILER [FHD] - YouTube
    Watch On

    A sprawling, influential melodrama, “Airport” depicts a snowstorm that paralyzes fictional Lincoln International Airport while a suicide bomber attempts to blow up a Boeing 707. A “cheesy antithesis of the frowning, arty groundswell of the ’70s,” the movie has a “certain magnificent cache,” said Ian Nathan at Empire. (Prime Video)

    ‘Titanic’ (1997)

    Titanic (1997) | Official Trailer - YouTube
    Watch On

    The most famous human-made catastrophe is brought to life in this award-winning epic that combines a doomed romance with a gorgeously rendered vision of the Titanic’s sinking. A “generous, compassionate spectacle,” it “turned into a cultural landmark and reference point,” said Brian Eggert at Deep Focus Review. (Paramount+)

    ‘The Wave’ (2015)

    Watch On

    A mountain crumbles into a Norwegian fjord and triggers a tsunami in this gripping film that places thousands in mortal peril. The movie makes the “most of the unique location, which lends itself to jaw-dropping vistas from every camera angle,” said The Hollywood Reporter. (Prime Video)

    ‘Don’t Look Up’ (2021)

    DON'T LOOK UP | Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Lawrence | Official Trailer | Netflix - YouTube
    Watch On

    A metaphor for our shambling response to climate change, this side-splitting satire looks at the warped incentives that lead global elites to deny the reality of a civilization-ending comet strike. “Narcissism and all that it has wrought, including the destruction of nature, will finally be our downfall,” said Manohla Dargis at The New York Times. (Netflix)
